title: AI-QCT plaque measurements associate with cardiovascular events in CONSERVE
summary: A post hoc analysis applied Cleerly AI-QCT to coronary CT images from 747 participants in the selective-referral arm of CONSERVE. Quantified plaque burden was associated with one-year major cardiovascular events; event rates increased across plaque-volume categories. Estimated reductions in invasive angiography and costs were hypothetical decision-model outputs, not observed effects of randomized AI-guided care. Stenosis-based event discrimination was similar to clinical readers, and no blinded quantitative angiography comparison was available.
organization: The George Washington University School of Medicine

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: Retrospective 747-patient plaque/event association and comparison with site CT interpretation.
evidence.unknown: AI-guided safety, realized catheterization reductions and cost savings were not tested prospectively.
evidence.ai_role: Validated CNNs perform image quality assessment, coronary segmentation, vascular measurement and plaque characterization. Post hoc analysis with hypothetical referral thresholds; randomized original cohort does not establish randomized AI benefit.
